name: Carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase 1 deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for urea cycle disorders

criteria.description: Presence of severe hyperammonemia with plasma ammonia levels >150 µmol/L
Reduced or absent carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase 1 enzyme activity in liver biopsy or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in the CPS1 gene by molecular genetic testing
Characteristic plasma amino acid profile showing low citrulline and elevated glutamine
Normal or low urinary orotic acid levels distinguishing CPS1 deficiency from ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hyperammonemia with confirmatory enzyme assay or pathogenic CPS1 gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent irreversible neurological damage.

laboratory: Normal or low urinary orotic acid
imaging: Brain MRI may show cerebral edema or demyelination in severe cases
other: Reduced CPS1 enzyme activity in liver biopsy or cultured fibroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated argininosuccinic acid in plasma and urine
Different enzyme deficiency in urea cycle

redFlags: Severe hyperammonemia (>150 µmol/L) without liver disease
references: Summar ML, et al. Urea cycle disorders overview. GeneReviews. 2020.
Häberle J, et al. Suggested guidelines for the diagnosis and management of urea cycle disorders. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2012.
Brusilow SW, Maestri NE. Urea cycle disorders: diagnosis, pathophysiology, and therapy. Adv Pediatr. 1996.
